conviction_note: A holding-company Q3 whose NAV is mostly computable from public 30 September marks (Aker BP +12% in Q3), with a dividend tranche the company already said it would pay and Nscale still carried at its March Series C price under the stated policy. Nothing decisive and unpriced was found, so p_up sits at 54 on a slight positive lean: NAV up, the discount wider at about 24%, a capital return coming, after a 21% Nscale-driven fall. abs_move 3.5 is set from the European pre-released base of about 3%, raised for 36.6% realised volatility and the AI-sentiment tape that now drives this name. The findings sum to +0.55 and the scaled number is +0.28; they agree in sign and both are small.

Q2 NAV NOK 106.1bn (NOK 1,429/share). findings.finding: Q3 NAV will rise about NOK 4-5bn on the Aker BP mark alone: 133.76m shares from NOK 303.2 at 30 Jun to 340.3 at 30 Sep, +NOK 4.96bn, less about NOK 0.7bn on Aker Solutions. That gives about NOK 1,490/share against spot 1,126, a ~24% discount versus 20% at Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAV-headline days moved +1.52 (Q3 25), -2.31 (Q4 25), +2.01 (Q1 26), -8.56 (Q2 26, with the BioMarine take-private the same morning); median 1.37 over 21 events
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: every NAV input is a public 30 Sep price and Aker's own policy says listed holdings are marked to market. Only a retail 'record NAV / wider discount' headline effect is left. If the market ignored it, the discount at spot would not already be visible from the Q2 table and the tape.
findings.independence: Aker BP tape https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AKRBP.OL?range=6mo&interval=1d (same arithmetic, different source)

findings.finding: An additional H2 cash dividend is pre-signalled for this release: the board said it would propose an authorisation 'in-line with previous years' practice'. Q3 2024 carried NOK 35.50 and Q3 2025 NOK 26.50, so the size, not the event, is the unknown; the ex-date falls after the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly unpriced on size only. The policy (4-6% of year-end NAV of NOK 67.3bn, i.e. NOK 2.7-4.0bn total, NOK 2.2bn already paid) and pending Cognite cash leave a range of about NOK 7-30+. A surprise either way would show as a move on a line that is otherwise inside guidance.

findings.finding: Under its stated NAV policy (most recent material third-party transaction), Aker should keep Nscale at the March Series C USD 14.6bn (NOK 32.1bn). The September USD 3.36bn pre-IPO round is a convertible priced at a discount to an IPO price not yet set, so the Q3 NAV carries no Nscale markdown even at the bearish USD 16-19bn IPO talk, while spot already implies a far lower value for the stake.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nscale-specific announcements: +7.1% on 2026-08-27 after the USD 45bn contract, -7.1% on 2026-10-19 on the IPO pushback report; the Q1 26 NAV re-mark day was +2.01
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from the policy text and is sized small. Market cap of about NOK 83.7bn against an ex-Nscale NAV of roughly NOK 79bn implies the market already discounts the stake heavily. If the market feared a markdown, the stock would trade above that implied stake value, not this far below the book mark.

findings.finding: Nscale was reported (Bloomberg via E24, 19 Oct) in talks over a second ~USD 45bn Anthropic contract at Monarch, 'possibly within days'. Aker has not announced it on NewsWeb, though it announced the August contract as inside information, so the release or webcast is a possible venue for confirmation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first USD 45bn Monarch contract (Aker inside-information release, 2026-08-26 after close) moved the stock +5.5% the next session (1484 -> 1566)
findings.original_quote: Ifølge Bloomberg kan avtalen komme på plass allerede i løpet av de neste dagene. Forhandlingene pågår fortsatt, og ingen endelig beslutning er tatt. [...] – Det ville vært rettferdiggjort om Aker-aksjen fikk rekyl etter denne avtalen, sier han til E24. (According to Bloomberg the deal could be in place within days; talks are ongoing and no final decision has been taken. 'A rebound in the Aker share would be justified after this deal.')
findings.why_not_priced: Talks are public, but a signing has not been confirmed by Aker or Nscale. One later trade report (DCD, 403 to both fetchers, snippet only) says it was signed. If the market held it as done, Aker would not have stayed at its post-19-Oct lows (1150-1180).

findings.finding: Nscale's operational headwinds (flagship Norway site six months behind schedule, Microsoft withdrawing from a site) and the IPO-valuation pushback will be the webcast's main Q&A. Management will be constrained by the SEC quiet period, so it can neither rebut nor confirm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 7.1% on 2026-10-19 when the pushback and delays were reported; -20.9% over 20 sessions
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the -21% run-up is this news. What remains is the risk that Aker discloses more detail on the Narvik delay, which was its own JV until the March roll-up. If it were unpriced, the stock would still sit near the late-September 1,440s.
